| [QUESTION-080](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-080.md) | When a trained network's parameters keep moving after its loss has converged, what about the network stays fixed, and is the last-layer geometry of neural collapse among the things that do? | The record holds two pictures of the end of training. In one, the last layer converges to a fixed geometry through the terminal phase ([THEORY-083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-083.md), neural collapse). In the other, the parameters never stop: they sample a stationary distribution at constant speed ([THEORY-209](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-209.md)). The two may describe different regimes. The terminal phase of neural collapse is cross-entropy training past zero error, with no finite minimum, while the limiting dynamics assume a quadratic minimum. Nothing in the record relates them. Drawn by the assistant from the reading of Kunin et al., and filed at the owner's request. | Open |
| [QUESTION-081](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-081.md) | When the relative scale of a network's layers sets its learning regime under gradient flow, does that regime survive SGD, whose minibatch noise drives the relative scale toward balance, and on what timescale compared with learning? | Two readings meet here. Under gradient flow, the relative scale of adjacent layers is conserved and sets whether learning is rich or lazy ([THEORY-212](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-212.md), Dominé et al.). Under SGD, that scale is not conserved: minibatch noise drives it toward the point where the layers' gradient noise balances, at a rate set by η/S ([THEORY-211](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-211.md), Ziyin et al.). If the drift is fast compared with learning, an unbalanced start chosen to be lazy would drift toward balance and richness. If it is slow, the regime set at initialization stands. | [QUESTION-211](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-211.md) | How far are independently trained latent spaces from a cosine-preserving map: is the held-out residual of the best orthogonal-times-scalar map close to that of the best linear map where anchor-based stitching works, and does the gap grow where it fails? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md). [THEORY-175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-175.md) was promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3) on its invariance, re-derived, and on what Moschella et al. measured: independently trained encoders agree in their cosine profiles to matched anchors only approximately, enough for untrained decoder transfer with loss, while their nearest neighbours mostly differ. The source never fits a map between two spaces. | Open |
| [QUESTION-216](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-216.md) | Does the output Fisher–Rao geometry agreement across language models replicate with released code, and does it fall when models are fitted to different laws while their activation geometry stays as it was, with only a small part of the shared eigenvector structure exceeding a fair law-matched null? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md). [THEORY-230](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-230.md) was narrowed and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2 and v3). Its identification is re-derived: the Fisher–Rao geometry of next-token laws is a function of the laws. Its measurement is one study read in full: mean rank agreement 0.88 against 0.62 in Picozzi's ten models, and about 9% of the top eigenvector overlap beyond a displacement-matched null. Replication, and a test that varies the law, are open. | Open |
| [QUESTION-217](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-217.md) v2 | When a learning system is said to go from coarse to fine, do the order in which its representations refine one another, the order of their relevance to a task and the order in which training acquires them admit one common chain, and under what conditions on the learning operator? | A1 and A2 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes. The record already holds that "coarse to fine" names different things: an order in training time by singular value ([THEORY-186](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-186.md)), an order in noise ([THEORY-199](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-199.md)), and a sample-complexity result in which every level arrives at once ([THEORY-195](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-195.md)). No entry separates refinement, relevance and acquisition as three relations and asks when they agree. An answer is a theorem giving sufficient conditions for a common chain, or a minimal family of counterexamples. | Open |
| [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md) v3 | Given that information-bottleneck optima at two budgets need not be nested, what condition on P(X, Y), beyond Y a function of X or X and Y both binary, guarantees that the coarser optimum is a (possibly noisy) function of the finer, X → Z₂ → Z₁, and how much is lost by forcing nesting when it fails? | A2 of the exchange of 2026-10-19 on coarse-to-fine processes, which called it "the most consequential missing bridge". A hierarchy of optimal abstractions needs more than an optimum at each budget: it needs the optima to be compatible. [NOTE-676](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-676.md) gets nesting by restricting the encoder to prunings of a fixed tree; nothing in the record says when it holds without that restriction. Rate–distortion theory's answer is successive refinability (Equitz and Cover, registered unread). | Open |
| [QUESTION-232](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-232.md) | Does the coarse-graining that maximizes mutual information with the system beyond a buffer find the renormalization-group variables of a system where they were not known beforehand, and does it give short-ranged effective Hamiltonians in two or more dimensions? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md), moved here when [THEORY-194](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-194.md) was narrowed to what Koch-Janusz and Ringel measured on the 2D Ising and dimer models and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3). Every 2D case in that study had a known answer, and the link to a short-ranged effective Hamiltonian is proved only for 1D and quasi-1D chains. | Open |
| [QUESTION-234](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-234.md) v3 | Do interchange interventions leave the mediating direction underdetermined in trained networks: do two basis-related alignments in a trained model tie on every interchange drawn from the data, and for which networks are alignments that agree on all such interventions unique up to a stated symmetry? | Filed when the promotion audit (batch 062, [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v2) narrowed and promoted [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) to what the constructed three-unit network proves: two basis-related alignments tie on every interchange intervention on the input. Whether such ties occur in trained networks, or are ruled out for some class up to a symmetry, was the old promote_when, and it moves here. | Open |
| [QUESTION-236](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-236.md) | Does fixed-feature transfer to new classes fall as penultimate class separation rises outside ImageNet-trained ResNet-50s, and does it move with within-class spread when the loss is held fixed? | The promotion condition formerly on [THEORY-246](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-246.md), moved unchanged when that account was narrowed to what Kornblith et al. (2021) measured and promoted on 2026-10-20 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v3). Open: whether the inverse relation between penultimate class separation and new-class transfer holds in other pretraining settings, and whether separation, rather than the loss, is what moves transfer. | Open |
| [QUESTION-244](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-244.md) | Must the optimal representations of an information-bottleneck objective at two budgets be nested, so that the coarser optimum is a (possibly noisy) function of the finer? | The yes-or-no part of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). No, for deterministic encoders ([CLAIM-387](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-387.md)) and for stochastic ones ([CLAIM-392](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-392.md)), on one four-state source with binary Y. Raising the budget can reorganize the optimum rather than split it. What condition on P(X, Y) guarantees nesting stays with [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-245](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-245.md) | For linear decisions at the population level, if a kind's admissible transformations are given as a distribution over pairs of its realizations, is the top eigenspace of the pair operator a stable, decision-sufficient span, and what span takes that role when the pairs are directed? | The linear part of [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). For symmetric pairs, yes: the top eigenfunctions are the most view-invariant directions, and their span is minimax-optimal for linear prediction of approximately view-invariant targets ([THEORY-007](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-007.md)) and bounds linear-probe error by leakage over conductance ([THEORY-228](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-228.md)). For directed pairs, the top left singular functions of the conditional-expectation operator take that role ([THEORY-239](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-239.md)), and a linear readout of the full density ratio suffices for redundant labels ([THEORY-319](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-319.md)). Other spans can tie. Nonlinear decisions, and what picks one signature out, stay with [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-274](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-274.md) v2 | Do two dictionaries of equal fidelity, trained on the same model with different seeds or widths, give the same validated circuit for the same prompt and behaviour, or is a feature circuit fixed only relative to the dictionary that supplies its units? | Feature circuits (sparse feature circuits, transcoder circuits, attribution graphs) are stated over the units of a learned dictionary. The dictionaries are not unique: features split and merge as the dictionary grows, and which concepts get a feature depends on their frequency relative to its size. Whether the circuit found for a behaviour survives a change of dictionary at equal fidelity is the question [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) asks of alignments, asked of dictionaries. No work the record holds has run the comparison. | Open |
| [QUESTION-275](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-275.md) | Can the development of a transformer's circuits in training be described as organizational regimes forming over shared, overlapping latent features, so that a model coupling feature allocation to circuit interaction, fitted to early checkpoints, predicts the effects of held-out training interventions that feature-only and circuit-only descriptions fitted to the same checkpoints miss? | The owner, at T24: "could we potentially apply this setup as an interpretive framework for understanding the learning dynamics of transformers?" "This setup" is the dynamic latent-feature model of T23 ([CASE-165](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-165.md)). The reply answered with a test: "Can the emergence, specialization, overlap, and persistence of transformer circuits be explained by modeling them as developing organizational regimes over shared latent features—and does that description predict training responses that existing feature- or circuit-based analyses miss?" It is the second time the owner has applied the record's frameworks to a network in training. The first was [CASE-113](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-113.md) and [CLAIM-367](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-367.md), and [CASE-117](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-117.md) is the population form. The sharp edge is [CLAIM-427](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-427.md)'s third grade: positive results would have to be prospective, against strong conventional baselines at matched complexity. Nothing here says that a circuit is a perspective. | Open |
| [QUESTION-286](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-286.md) | Under smooth invertible changes of the parameter coordinates, which first-order frustration diagnoses among a learner's demands are invariant: pairwise Euclidean gradient angles, common strict first-order descent, or budgeted feasibility with the update geometry transported? | The coordinate part of [QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) (Active) settles it in full. Common strict descent, 0 ∉ conv{g_i}, is invariant under smooth invertible reparameterization. The sign of a Euclidean gradient inner product is not, and a negative inner product does not exclude common descent. A budgeted test is invariant when the metric is pulled back. These are the first three rows of A35 §2's table. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-291](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-291.md) | For finite X and Y, does every finite-budget information-bottleneck optimum nest under the β → ∞ optimum, what test on a pair of optimal encoders decides whether two finite budgets nest, and do the optima nest at every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X or when X and Y are both binary? | The settled part of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md), [THEORY-753](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md) and [THEORY-757](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-757.md) (Active) answer it. Every finite-β optimum is a stochastic coarsening of the causal partition. Two budgets nest iff some pair of optimal encoders forms X → T₂ → T₁, a convex-hull test on decoder points. The optima nest at every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X and when X and Y are both binary. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-294](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-294.md) | When a network's architecture can represent a structured system's renormalization step exactly, must training by distribution fitting make the variables it represents the system's relevant ones? | The representability part of [QUESTION-060](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-060.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) (Active) settles it, in the negative. Mehta and Schwab's RBM–renormalization correspondence is an identity of parametrizations, and an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution. Away from that point a contrastive-divergence RBM spends its hidden units on noise, not on the relevant fields. The architecture's match does not fix what training keeps. | Answered |
